title: Chest Pain

rationale.ECG: No P waves, irregularly irregular, narrow QRS. AFib.
rationale.Echo: Valvular disease, LA size, LV function.
rationale.Anticoagulation (DOAC / Warfarin): Per CHA2DS2-VASc. DOAC preferred over warfarin.
rationale.Cardioversion if symptomatic: If <48h → cardiovert. If >48h → TEE first or 3 weeks AC first.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with palpitations, irregularly irregular pulse, dizziness, fatigue, and chest discomfort. ECG shows no P waves, irregularly irregular R-R intervals with narrow QRS. May have rapid ventricular response (RVR). AFib is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia. Causes: HTN, CAD, valvular disease, CHF, hyperthyroidism, alcohol, PE, post-op, lone AFib. Classification: paroxysmal (<7d), persistent (>7d), long-standing persistent (>1yr), permanent. Management priorities: (1) Rate control: beta-blocker (metoprolol) or CCB (diltiazem/verapamil), target HR <110. (2) Anticoagulation: CHA2DS2-VASc score — if ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women → anticoagulation (DOAC preferred over warfarin). If <2, no anticoagulation. (3) Rhythm control if symptomatic despite rate control: cardioversion (electrical or pharmacological — flecainide, amiodarone). If AFib <48h → safe to cardiovert. If >48h or unknown → TEE to rule out LAA thrombus first, or anticoagulate x3 weeks before cardioversion. Anticoagulate x4 weeks post-cardioversion.
